concept: GGUF re-upload versioning and stale cache hygiene
summary: Hugging Face cache layout: `blobs/` holds files named by hash; `refs/<branch>` holds the commit hash currently seen for that ref; `snapshots/<commit>/` holds symlinks to blobs, one folder per revision ever fetched. An unchanged file is shared between revisions through the same blob.

facts.text: Hugging Face cache layout: `blobs/` holds files named by hash; `refs/<branch>` holds the commit hash currently seen for that ref; `snapshots/<commit>/` holds symlinks to blobs, one folder per revision ever fetched. An unchanged file is shared between revisions through the same blob.

When a repo is updated at the same filename, the next `hf download` of main resolves a new commit, writes a new `snapshots/<new-commit>/` folder and updates `refs/main`; the old snapshot and its blobs stay on disk until deleted. So a re-upload doubles disk use for each changed GGUF until pruned.

`hf cache ls --revisions` lists per-revision snapshots; `hf cache verify <repo>` checks cached file checksums; `hf cache rm <id>` deletes an entry; `hf cache prune` is listed without a stated scope on the page read (for Xet it removes shared files no cached repo uses); filters such as `--filter "size>30g"` and `--filter "accessed>1y"` select entries.

Pinning: `hf download <repo> --revision <commit|branch|tag>` fetches a fixed revision; `resolve_revision()` resolves main to a commit once so multiple files come from one commit, because two calls seconds apart can land on different commits if the repo changes in between.

Xet-backed files are stored once per content hash across repos (shared blobs), so identical bytes in two repos cost one copy; older clients (including llama.cpp and anything that follows symlinks) can delete a shared file that other repos still use, forcing a re-download.
llama.cpp `-hf` uses its own cache directory; `LLAMA_CACHE` selects where it saves.
Unsloth Studio/Desktop reuses already-present GGUF files instead of downloading again whenever a model loads, so a stale file persists unless the user removes it.
2026-03-05: Unsloth docs banner "Redownload Qwen3.5 35B, 27B, 122B and 397B"; the only notice is a dated line on a guide page.
2026-03-27 / 2026-04-01: Unsloth Studio starts detecting models already in the HF cache and LM Studio folders; then lets users select an existing folder.
2026-05-18: Unsloth Studio warns when its bundled llama.cpp prebuilt is stale or too old for MTP.
2026-07-20: Unsloth reuses existing GGUF files whenever a model loads.
2026-08-19: Qwen3.8-27B Dynamic v3.0 update: non-dynamic files such as `Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf` were deleted from the repo; an `MTP` folder appeared.
2026-09-22: Studio can reuse downloaded models without duplicate copies and inspect or clear caches in Settings.

Partial update: after the Qwen3.8 v3 re-upload a user reported `UD-Q8_K_XL` "wasn't updated or included in the benchmarks"; one repo can hold files from different generations, so checking the commit date of each file matters, not the repo's last-modified time.

Embedded chat template not refreshed: users reported later in the same thread that the new GGUFs still raised `Jinja Exception: System message must be at the beginning.` with Claude Code (HTTP 500 from llama-server), pointing at an earlier discussion (42) that carried the template fix.

Preview versus final under one name: a user reported the final Dynamic v3 UD 2-bit-XL did worse than the earlier preview v3 file on a coding test (anecdote), which shows that "update" can regress for a given workload and the old file is no longer downloadable by name.
Deleted variants: a plain Q4_K_M that a script referenced by filename disappears and a `-hf repo:Q4_K_M` style reference may then fail or resolve to a different file (inferred, not reported).

mmproj mismatch: the vision projector is a separate GGUF, not versioned with the text GGUF; a wrong or stale one fails at load with `mtmd_init_from_file: error: mismatch between text model (n_embd = 2816) and mmproj (n_embd = 1536)`.
Desktop uninstall does not clean models: removing the app (or `~/.unsloth/studio`) leaves HF model files in `~/.cache/huggingface/hub/` and LM Studio models in their own folder.
Stuck downloads: Unsloth documents a Hugging Face Hub Xet debugging section for stalled downloads and ships an HTTP fallback for stalled downloads in its core package.

Whether a re-upload is a fix: Unsloth's pinned thread says "nothing was broken" and the update was "purely an update to make them EVEN BETTER" (existing file); users in the same thread report a template error that persisted and a regression versus the preview. Both are reported; the vendor does not publish per-file changelogs or hashes.
No source says how LM Studio or Ollama detect a changed upstream GGUF (LM Studio keeps its own `lm-studio/models` store, which Unsloth Studio says llama.cpp cannot see by default).
No source lists a stable machine-readable version marker for Unsloth GGUF re-uploads; the HF commit hash and per-file sha256 are the only handles.
The Hugging Face cache stores files in `blobs/` named by hash, branch-to-commit mappings in `refs/`, and one `snapshots/<commit>/` folder per fetched revision containing symlinks to blobs.
A file unchanged between two revisions shares one blob, so it is not downloaded again when the second revision is fetched.
Re-downloading from a reference after the repo head changes updates the `refs/<ref>` file to the new commit hash.

`HfApi.resolve_revision()` resolves a branch to a commit once so many file downloads use one commit; two per-file resolutions seconds apart can land on different commits if the repo is updated in between.
The revision-to-commit mapping is written into `refs/`, so a later offline resolve can use it.
Xet files are deduplicated across repos in the cache, with each repo blob a relative symlink to one shared blob.

Older clients including llama.cpp and anything that follows symlinks keep reading normally, but their cache-deletion tools may delete a shared file other repos still use; the fix is an up-to-date `huggingface_hub` for `hf cache rm` and `hf cache prune`.
`HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1` disables the shared store and `HF_HUB_DISABLE_SHARED_BLOBS=1` opts out of cross-repo sharing.
`hf cache` offers `ls`, `ls --revisions`, `rm`, `prune` and `verify`; `hf cache ls` accepts filters such as `size>30g` and `accessed>1y` and `-q` for IDs that can be piped to `hf cache rm`.
`hf download --revision` accepts a commit hash, branch or tag.
Unsloth's Qwen3.5 guide carries "Mar 5 Update: Redownload Qwen3.5-35B, 27B, 122B and 397B".
Unsloth's guides tell users to `export LLAMA_CACHE="folder"` to force llama.cpp to save a model to a chosen location.

Unsloth Studio detects models downloaded to the Hugging Face hub cache; LM Studio GGUFs in `~/.cache/lm-studio/models` or `~/lm-studio/models` are not visible to llama.cpp by default and must be copied into the HF cache or another path.
Unsloth Studio added automatic detection of existing models on 2026-03-27 and a user-selected existing-folder option on 2026-04-01.
Unsloth's July 20 2026 changelog says existing GGUF files are reused instead of being downloaded again whenever a model loads.
Unsloth's May 18 2026 changelog says Studio warns when the bundled llama.cpp prebuilt is stale or too old for MTP.
Unsloth's September 22 2026 changelog says reuse of downloaded models avoids duplicate copies and that caches can be inspected or cleared from Settings.
Unsloth's uninstall steps for Studio and Desktop do not touch downloaded HF model files; the default location is `~/.cache/huggingface/hub/` unless `HF_HUB_CACHE` or `HF_HOME` is set.
In the pinned Qwen3.8-27B thread a user noted the non-dynamic `Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf` files were deleted.
In the same thread a user asked why `UD-Q8_K_XL` was not updated and said it still had the broken Jinja template.
A user reported llama-server error `Jinja Exception: System message must be at the beginning.` with Claude Code on the new GGUFs and linked an earlier discussion that carried the template fix.
A user reported the final Dynamic v3 UD 2-bit-XL did worse than the older preview v3 build on one coding task (single anecdote).
llama.cpp refuses an mmproj whose embedding size differs from the text model with `mtmd_init_from_file: error: mismatch between text model (n_embd = 2816) and mmproj (n_embd = 1536)`.
Unsloth's Gemma 4 guide points stalled Hugging Face downloads to a Xet debugging section.
After any vendor re-upload, run `hf cache ls --revisions`, delete older snapshots with `hf cache rm`, and verify with `hf cache verify`, since only the commit hash differs.
For reproducible Mac benchmarks, pin `--revision <commit>` and record each GGUF's sha256 next to results.
